newsitem.title: USA: NYSEG board rejects CalEnergy offer.
newsitem.headline: NYSEG board rejects CalEnergy offer.

text.p: New York State Electric & Gas Corp. on Wednesday rejected CalEnergy Co. Inc.'s unsolicited tender offer to purchase NYSEG common stock for about $160 million, bringing its total ownership to 9.9 percent.

CalEnergy, based in Omaha, Neb., offered to buy about 6.5 million shares of stock for $24.50 per share in cash. Added to the shares CalEnergy already owns, the purchase would give CalEnergy 9.9 percent of NYSEG.

NYSEG said the board also rejected CalEnergy's proposal to begin negotiations on the acquisition of all of NYSEG at $27.50 per share, for a total of about $1.9 billion. The Binghamton, N.Y.-based utility said the purchase was not in the best interests of the company or its shareholders, customers and employees.
CalEnergy said it remained committed to its plan to acquire NYSEG.

"We intend to pursue this transaction in spite of the board's decision, complete our 9.9 percent tender offer and move forward aggressively on our NYSEG acquisition plan," CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol said in a statement.
CalEnergy last December acquired Britain's Northern Electric Plc for $1.3 billion with the support of a slim majority of the British utility's shareholders.
CalEnergy currently operates 19 generating facilities and supplies and distributes electricity.
NYSEG said the $27.50-per-share offer that CalEnergy said it was willing to pay for the entire company was inadequate.
CalEnergy stock fell 19 cents to $40.44 and NYSEG rose 6 cents to $25.25, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
